subtitle: Lesson 17 · Core ITIL 4 Practices: Incident, Problem & Change

code:
1. Incident logged -> resolved (maybe a workaround)
2. Recurs or cause unclear -> problem opened
3. Root cause found, no fix yet -> known error
4. Fix needs a config/code change -> change
   enablement (normal or emergency)
5. Change implemented -> known error closes
6. Future incidents from that cause stop
caption: Three practices, one continuous flow.

steps.label: Incident management
steps.sub: keeps the business running every time the symptom recurs

steps.label: Problem management
steps.sub: finds the real cause, but has no authority to change production

steps.label: Change enablement
steps.sub: assesses risk and authorizes the fix before it's implemented

code:
Diagnosing a cause != authority to fix it.

Known error (problem management's output)
        |
        v
Change request (must go through change
enablement, regardless of who found the cause)
caption: This is the single most-missed link between the three practices.
